questions.enonce_markdown:
The table below shows the population $P$, in thousands and to one decimal place, of a certain town $T$ years after 1980.

| $T$ | 1 | 3 | 5 | 7 | 9 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $P$ | 17.8 | 63.1 | 223.9 | 707.9 | 2511.9 |

It is believed that $P$ and $T$ are connected by a law of the form

$$P = ab^T.$$

By plotting $\log P$ against $T$, estimate to one decimal place, the values of the constants $a$ and $b$.

Hence, state the approximate population of this town in 1980. (9 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Reducing the law to linear form.** Take logarithms to base $10$ of $P = ab^T$:

$$\log P = \log a + T\log b.$$

This is of the form $Y = c + mT$ with $Y = \log P$, so a graph of $\log P$ (vertical axis) against $T$ (horizontal axis) is a straight line with

$$\text{gradient} = \log b, \qquad \text{vertical intercept (at } T = 0) = \log a.$$

**Table of values** (base-10 logarithms, 3 decimal places):

| $T$ | 1 | 3 | 5 | 7 | 9 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $P$ | 17.8 | 63.1 | 223.9 | 707.9 | 2511.9 |
| $\log P$ | 1.250 | 1.800 | 2.350 | 2.850 | 3.400 |

**The graph.** Draw axes with $T$ from $0$ to $10$ (e.g. $2\ \mathrm{cm}$ per unit) and $\log P$ from $0$ to $3.5$ (e.g. $4\ \mathrm{cm}$ per unit; start the vertical axis at $0$ so that the intercept at $T = 0$ can be read). Plot the five points $(1, 1.250)$, $(3, 1.800)$, $(5, 2.350)$, $(7, 2.850)$, $(9, 3.400)$. They lie very close to a straight line, which confirms the law $P = ab^T$. Draw the line of best fit, extended back to the vertical axis. It passes through the mean point $(\bar T, \overline{\log P}) = (5,\ 2.33)$.

**Reading the line of best fit.** For the line of best fit, the points $(1, 1.25)$ and $(9, 3.40)$ near its ends give

$$\text{gradient} \approx \frac{3.40 - 1.25}{9 - 1} = \frac{2.15}{8} \approx 0.269,$$

and the least-squares line through all five points has gradient $0.2675$ and intercept $0.993$. So, reading from the graph,

$$\log b \approx 0.27 \;\Longrightarrow\; b = 10^{0.27} \approx 1.86 \approx 1.9,$$

$$\log a \approx 0.99 \;\Longrightarrow\; a = 10^{0.99} \approx 9.8.$$

$$\boxed{a \approx 9.8, \qquad b \approx 1.9}$$

(Graphical estimates from a hand-drawn line vary slightly: values of $a$ between about $9.5$ and $10$ and of $b$ about $1.9$ are consistent with the data.)

**Law and population in 1980.** The law is $P \approx 9.8 \times 1.9^{\,T}$ (in thousands). The year 1980 corresponds to $T = 0$, where $P = ab^0 = a$. Hence the population in 1980 was approximately $9.8$ thousand:

$$\boxed{P(0) = a \approx 9.8 \text{ thousand} \approx 9\,800 \text{ people}}$$

Check: with $a = 9.84$ and $b = 1.85$ the law gives $P(5) = 9.84 \times 1.85^5 \approx 213$ against the observed $223.9$, $P(7) \approx 733$ against $707.9$ and $P(9) = 9.84 \times 1.85^9 \approx 2\,498$ against $2\,511.9$: the fit is reasonable, as the data are only approximately of this form.
